arxiv-2007-15043.title: Non-Uniform Sampling of Fixed Margin Binary Matrices
arxiv-2007-15043.creator: Alex Fout, Bailey K. Fosdick, Matthew P. Hitt
arxiv-2007-15043.description: Abstract Data sets in the form of binary matrices are ubiquitous across scientific domains, and researchers are often interested in identifying and quantifying noteworthy structure. One approach is to compare the observed data to that which might be obtained under a null model.

arxiv-2108-06517.title: Characterizing the free-energy landscapes of DNA origamis
arxiv-2108-06517.creator: Chak Kui Wong, Chuyan Tang, John S. Schreck, Jonathan P. K. Doye
arxiv-2108-06517.description: Abstract We show how coarse-grained modelling combined with umbrella sampling using distance-based order parameters can be applied to compute the free-energy landscapes associated with mechanical deformations of large DNA nanostructures. We illustrate this approach for the strong bending of DNA nanotubes and the potentially bistable landscape of twisted DNA origami sheets.

arxiv-2211-11350.title: Rooms with Text: A Dataset for Overlaying Text Detection
arxiv-2211-11350.creator: Oleg Smirnov, Aditya Tewari
arxiv-2211-11350.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a new dataset of room interior pictures with overlaying and scene text, totalling to 4836 annotated images in 25 product categories. We provide details on the collection and annotation process of our dataset, and analyze its statistics.

arxiv-2404-04190.title: The link between 1 1 -norm approximation and effective Positivstellensatze for the hypercube
arxiv-2404-04190.creator: Etienne de Klerk, Juan C. Vera
arxiv-2404-04190.description: Abstract The Schmüdgen Positivstellensatz gives a certificate to verify positivity of a strictly positive polynomial f f on a compact, basic, semi-algebraic set 𝐊 ⊂ ℝ n \mathbf{K}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{n} . A Positivstellensatz of this type is called effective if one may bound the degrees of the polynomials appearing in the certificate in terms of properties of f f .

arxiv-2408-04688.title: Size Should Not Matter: Evaluating Network Visualizations with Stress
arxiv-2408-04688.creator: Reyan Ahmed, Cesim Erten, Stephen Kobourov, Jonah Lotz, Jacob Miller, Hamlet Taraz
arxiv-2408-04688.description: Abstract The normalized stress metric is widely used to assess graph drawing quality, measuring how closely distances between vertices in a layout match their graph-theoretic distances. This metric is a standard for both evaluation and optimization in many popular graph layout algorithms.

arxiv-2410-13078.title: A Topos-Theoretic Semantics of Intuitionistic Modal Logic with an Application to the Logic of Branching Spacetime
arxiv-2410-13078.creator: Michael J. Lambert
arxiv-2410-13078.description: Abstract The Alexandrov topology affords a well-known semantics of modal necessity and possibility. This paper develops an Alexandrov topological semantics of intuitionistic propositional modal logic internally in any elementary topos. This is done by constructing interior and closure operators on the power-object associated to a given relation in the ambient topos.

pmc-11600597.title: The intratumoral landscape of T cell receptor repertoire in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-11600597.creator: Meng Yang, Dan He, Yu Sun, Yunquan Guo, Yu Ma, Lin Feng, Meng Liu
pmc-11600597.description: BackgroundEsophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a malignant neoplasm with detrimental implications for human health. The landscape of ESCC therapy has been revolutionized by the introduction of immunotherapy, specifically involving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). A number of studies have documented the prognostic significance of T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire and its association with many tumors.

pmc-12751634.title: Advanced machine learning techniques for coronary artery disease risk prediction in early middle-aged adults
pmc-12751634.creator: Georgios Ntritsos, Erez Ornan, Eran Feldhay, Gil Chernin, Evangelos Evangelou
pmc-12751634.description: BackgroundCoronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of death globally, with early risk prediction being vital for timely intervention. In this study we utilized advanced machine learning techniques, incorporating clinical, lifestyle, and Genetic factors with the aim to enhance the 10-year risk prediction of CAD in early middle-aged adults (40–55 years).

pmc-13318489.creator: Hugo G Quezada-Pinedo, Tyson Brown, Ene M Enogela, Emily B Levitan, Oluwasegun P Akinyelure, Valerie A Smith, Laura C Pinheiro, Monika M Safford, Ro-Jay Reid, Tomi F Akinyemiju, C Barrett Bowling, Lewis A Lipsitz
pmc-13318489.description: BackgroundStructural racism contributes to health inequities in the United States. This study aimed to quantify the association between state racism index (SRI) and physical function.MethodsIn a national United States community-based cohort study, 13 661 non-Hispanic Black and White adults who had baseline information (2003-2007), SRI data (2006-2010) and physical function data (2013-2016) were included.

pmc-13371556.title: Integrating ChatGPT into nursing education: a randomized trial exploring knowledge, retention, and student perspectives on endotracheal suctioning
pmc-13371556.creator: Emine Sezgunsay, Ahmet Berkay Polat, Sude Bengisu Kılıcer
pmc-13371556.description: AimThis study aimed to evaluate the preliminary effectiveness of a ChatGPT-integrated educational session on nursing students’ knowledge acquisition and retention regarding endotracheal suctioning, and to explore their perspectives and learning experiences.MethodsA pilot pre-test/post-test parallel-group randomized controlled trial with an embedded qualitative component was conducted with 32 undergraduate nursing students who participated voluntarily.

pmc-13384134.title: Implementing and evaluating Adaptive Mentorship Networks to strengthen primary care in Canada: protocol for a mixed-methods implementation science study
pmc-13384134.creator: Arun Radhakrishnan, L Jayne Beselt, Alesha C King, Zachary van Allen, Douglas Archibald, Jerry Maniate, Samuel Hickcox, Cristian Rangel, Joshua A Rash
pmc-13384134.description: AbstractIntroductionCanada’s health workforce crisis is placing sustained pressure on primary care, particularly in the management of chronic pain, mental health conditions and substance use disorders. Mentoring is a compelling response to workforce, educational and well-being challenges in healthcare, and Adaptive Mentorship Networks (AMNs) have emerged in Canada as an interprofessional model to strengthen provider capacity, psychological safety and compassionate care.

pmc-13495076.title: A novel enhanced triboelectric nanogenerator based on interlocking micro/nanostructures
pmc-13495076.creator: Boyu Zheng, Renwen Chen, Xintong Hou, Peng Wang, Junyi Zhang
pmc-13495076.description: SummaryTriboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) convert mechanical energy through contact electrification and electrostatic induction, with performance strongly affected by interfacial topography. Here, we report an interlocking micro/nanostructure-enhanced TENG (ILMS-TENG) fabricated by femtosecond-laser ablation of aluminum and nanoimprinting of complementary PDMS features. The size-matched interlocking interface increases the real contact area and improves charge separation.

pmc-13556360.title: 271. Glymphatic system dysfunction, accelerated brain aging, and inflammation in major psychiatric disorders: a transdiagnostic DTI-ALPS study
pmc-13556360.creator: Y M Bai, AC-C Yang, M-H Chen, S-J Tsai
pmc-13556360.description: BackgroundMajor psychiatric disorders, including Schizophrenia (SZ), Bipolar Disorder (BD), and Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), are increasingly recognized as conditions associated with accelerated biological aging and cognitive decline. The glymphatic system, a glial-dependent perivascular network, mediated by aquaporin-4 (AQP4) channels, plays a critical role in clearing metabolic waste and soluble proteins from the central nervous system.

pmc-13620180.title: Long-Standing Hypokalemia and Hypomagnesemia in a 61 Year-Old Woman: A Delayed Diagnosis of Gitelman Syndrome
pmc-13620180.creator: Shin Young Lee, Sang-Woong Han, Jiwon Lee, Mi-Yeon Yu
pmc-13620180.description: BackgroundGitelman syndrome (GS) is an autosomal recessive renal tubular disorder characterized by a distinct biochemical profile, including hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesemia, and hypocalciuria. Due to its often mild or nonspecific clinical presentation, GS is frequently misdiagnosed as idiopathic hypokalemia, leading to prolonged symptomatic treatment without a definitive etiologic diagnosis.

pmc-13672727.title: Comparative investigation of extended-gate GaAsSb/InGaAs HTFET biosensors for label-free biomolecule detection
pmc-13672727.creator: Mahin Anjum, Md. Mehedi Hasan, Md. Feroz Ali, Md Shafiul Alam, Obaidullah Obaidi
pmc-13672727.description: The dielectric-modulated heterostructure tunnel FET (HTFET)-based nano-cavity integrated biosensors are emerging as energy-efficient, ultra-sensitive label-free detection platforms. This study investigates and compares three GaAsSb/InGaAs-based biosensor architectures: single cavity dual material double composite gate HTFET (SC-DM-DG HTFET), dual cavity dual material double composite gate HTFET (DC-DM-DG HTFET), and single cavity dual material extended double composite gate HTFET (SC-DM-EDG HTFET).
